topStories.headline: Glen Park Gets a Say on Dangerous Freeway Ramps — Public Input Open Through December 18
topStories.dek: The SF County Transportation Authority is asking Glen Park residents to weigh in on safety fixes at three I-280 ramp intersections with a history of collisions.
topStories.body:
The San Francisco County Transportation Authority posted a call for public input on November 11, asking residents — including those in Glen Park — to complete a survey on its Vision Zero Freeway Ramps Study. The study focuses on safety improvements at eleven intersections where freeway ramps meet local streets in the south and southeast of the city, three of which sit squarely in the Glen Park and Outer Mission area: the I-280 ramp at Monterey Boulevard, the I-280 southbound ramp at San Jose Avenue and Sadowa Street, and the I-280 northbound ramp at Alemany and San Jose.

The study aims to design both quick-build and longer-term improvements at locations that have a documented history of crashes and appear on the city's Vision Zero High Injury Network. The Transportation Authority is accepting feedback via online surveys in English, Spanish, Chinese, and Tagalog at sfcta.org/vzramps. The survey remains open until December 18.

For residents who prefer an in-person session, the agency has scheduled a community block party specifically covering the Glen Park and Outer Mission ramps for Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to noon at Ocean Avenue and Plymouth Avenue. A second session focused on Mission and Potrero ramps will follow on Wednesday, November 18, from 5 to 7 p.m. at Potrero Hill Neighborhood House.

The Glen Park Association flagged the SFCTA request on its website the same day the agency published it, encouraging neighbors to participate. The Transportation Authority says it will use community input to develop draft designs and return for a second round of public engagement before bringing the final study to its board for adoption.

topStories.headline: Supervisor-Elect McCoy Now Waits for December Certification Before Taking District 8 Seat
topStories.dek: Gary McCoy won the November 3 vote decisively, but San Francisco won't issue certified results until December 3 — with his swearing-in expected in January.
topStories.body:
Ten days after election night, Gary McCoy's victory in the District 8 supervisor race has only grown more emphatic with each ballot update. The latest ranked-choice tally from the San Francisco Department of Elections shows McCoy finishing with roughly 63 percent of the vote after all rounds, well ahead of runner-up Darshini Patel. The department will not issue certified results until December 3.

McCoy, a former political director for Rep. Nancy Pelosi and a recovery advocate who spent years at the addiction-treatment nonprofit HealthRIGHT 360, bested Patel and Michael Nguyen to claim the seat being vacated by termed-out Supervisor Rafael Mandelman. Mandelman will leave office in January, at which point McCoy is expected to be sworn in. District 8 covers the Castro, Noe Valley, Duboce Triangle, Glen Park, Diamond Heights, and Cole Valley.

Political analysts are already watching to see what kind of swing vote McCoy becomes on a Board of Supervisors that has largely aligned with Mayor Daniel Lurie. McCoy backed elements of Lurie's public-safety agenda on the campaign trail — including the RESET Center as a drug-use alternative to jail — but his broader platform, which includes filling empty storefronts, building thousands of new homes, and a block-by-block approach to homelessness outreach, resists easy categorization. As the SF Chronicle noted, he received endorsements from both moderates and progressives, leaving his exact role on the board an open question.

McCoy has described his personal history with addiction and housing instability as central to how he will approach the district's most urgent issues. 'I made a decision to be very public about my recovery, and District 8 took a chance on that,' he said at his election-night party.

topStories.headline: Castro Theatre's November Is a Marathon — Sold-Out Nights and a Story Championship This Week
topStories.dek: The renovated Castro Theatre is running nearly every night this month, with The Moth GrandSLAM Championship sold out tonight and a string of concerts through the end of November.
topStories.body:
The Castro Theatre's fall calendar is as dense as it has ever been since the venue reopened in February after a $41 million renovation. November alone features close to two dozen ticketed events, and multiple shows have already sold out, with some acts adding extra nights to meet demand.

Tonight, Friday November 13, the venue hosts The Moth GrandSLAM Championship — the ultimate round of the storytelling series in which winners of the city's open-mic StorySLAMs return to compete for the San Francisco GrandSLAM title. Doors open at 7 p.m. and the show begins at 8 p.m. The event is listed as sold out at thecastro.com, though resale tickets may still be available through third-party sellers.

The week ahead at 429 Castro Street includes country-soul artist Paul Cauthen on Saturday the 14th, Rodrigo y Gabriela on Sunday the 15th, and British R&B singer Jorja Smith on Monday the 16th. Hamilton Leithauser and Rostam bring their joint tour to the stage on Wednesday the 18th, followed by Indian singer-songwriter Prateek Kuhad on the 19th. Later in the month, BERTHA: Grateful Drag takes the stage on the 21st and the Academy SF's annual Legends Awards celebration returns on Sunday the 22nd.

The venue's programming mix — concerts, storytelling, drag, comedy, and community events — reflects the broader vision Another Planet Entertainment has pursued since taking over operations in 2022. Tickets and the full calendar are at thecastro.com.

moreNews.headline: New Cafe Jandii Expected to Open This Month at 3499 16th Street in the Castro
moreNews.body: Jandii Cafe is listed as opening in November 2026 at 3499 16th Street in the Castro, according to WhatsOpening, a commercial real-estate tracking site. No further details about the concept or ownership have been publicly confirmed. Neighbors walking by the address can check the window for signage as the opening approaches.

moreNews.headline: Glen Park Rec Center Small Field Closed Through November 23 for Turf Restoration
moreNews.body: The small field behind the Glen Park Recreation Center has been closed for turf restoration since October 19 and is scheduled to reopen on Monday, November 23, according to the Glen Park Association. The main rec center facilities remain open during the closure.

moreNews.headline: San Francisco Voters Approve Proposition B, Paving the Way for a City-Owned Public Bank
moreNews.body: Proposition B, which would create a city-owned financing corporation as a first step toward a public bank, passed with roughly 52.6 percent of the vote in the November 3 election, according to updated tallies as of November 10. District 8 — where the Castro and Noe Valley gave the measure significant support — was among the higher-turnout districts in the city. Certified results from the San Francisco Department of Elections are due December 3.
